nodes.label: Use streaming/chunked reads + hash-narrowing instead of a PySpark cluster
nodes.rationale: At 200-300M rows the validator can't hold full source+target+result in memory. Rather than adopting a Spark cluster (new infra, would require re-proving correctness rules like dup-key/PK-less/JSON-hstore canonicalization in Spark's API), stream reads in bounded chunks per connector and use a cheap hash pre-filter (Tier 1) to narrow expensive exact Python comparison (Tier 2) to only disagreeing rows. Rejected chunked-fetch-only (still moves 100% of bytes through compare stage) and DB-side hashing as final answer (no SQL dialect reproduces Python-side JSON/decimal canonicalization identically across all four sources) — hash used only as a safe pre-filter.
nodes.norm_label: use streaming/chunked reads + hash-narrowing instead of a pyspark cluster

nodes.label: Parallelize table-level validation with a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor
nodes.rationale: Project/main.py validated tables strictly sequentially even though tables are independent (separate connections/output files). Decision: run tables concurrently via a bounded concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor (MAX_TABLE_WORKERS, default 4) because per-table work is I/O-bound (network round-trips), not CPU-bound, so the GIL releases during waits. Rejected multiprocessing (no benefit since bottleneck is I/O not CPU, would need file-locking instead of threading.Lock) and asyncio (bigger surface change across every Project/db/*.py connector for the same win threads already give). Required extracting _validate_table() to avoid non-atomic += across threads, and adding threading.Lock() around shared summary/audit file writes.
nodes.norm_label: parallelize table-level validation with a bounded threadpoolexecutor

nodes.label: Where AI is actually used: YAML generation vs. Run Validation (investigation)
nodes.rationale: Investigation-only: confirmed by grep that Run Validation (webapp -> runner.start_validation() -> subprocess python main.py) contains zero AI imports/calls anywhere in Project/ — Python-only, matching the stated client claim. The '[SQLQueryGenerator] AI generation active' log line instead comes from YAML generation (SQLQueryGenerator.__init__ in src/generated_queries/sql_query_generator.py), printed once per table when QueryOutputManager builds a SQLQueryGenerator, unrelated to Run Validation timing coincidence in the console. Flagged a separate real discrepancy: SQLQueryGenerator hard-fails on use_ai=False, meaning the SQL-text-generation step is AI-mandatory for every table, not just for resolving ambiguous column names — narrower/different from the old fully-removed 100%-AI ai_transformation/orchestrator.py pattern, but still broader than the 'AI only for ambiguous columns' claim.

nodes.label: Fix: Run Validation stuck on Running forever (subprocess pipe deadlock)
nodes.rationale: Root cause: switching Project/runner.py from subprocess.run(capture_output=True) (which drains pipes concurrently via internal threads) to a pollable subprocess.Popen + proc.communicate() (only read at the end, gated on proc.poll()) for the Stop-button feature, introduced a classic pipe deadlock — main.py's DEBUG-level SQL logging fills the ~64KB OS pipe buffer, the child blocks on write(), and the parent never sees poll() report exit because the child never exits while blocked. Fix: redirect child stdout/stderr to temp files (unbounded, no blocking) instead of subprocess.PIPE, wrapped in a RunningValidation dataclass; applied to both the Stop-button path and the scheduler's blocking run_validation() path, since both had the identical bug.
nodes.norm_label: fix: run validation stuck on running forever (subprocess pipe deadlock)
